content: 1. Lurasidone and mifepristone may increase each other's levels by interfering with the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Mifepristone and maprotiline can both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 3. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of mavorixafor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Both mifepristone and mavorixafor can prolong the QTc interval, and mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as co-administered medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other QTc-prolonging drugs. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 5. Mifepristone and mefloquine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 6. Mifepristone decreases the effects of mestranol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 7. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of metaxalone by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. 8. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of methadone by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9, so the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. The combination may also increase the QT interval. Alternatives should be considered if available. 9. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of mirtazapine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of mirvetuximab soravtansine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4 (a cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 11. Mitotane decreases the levels of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for potential dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 12. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of modafinil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of intranasal mometasone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Mifepristone and moxifloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 15. Nafcillin decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 16. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of naldemedine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Nefazodone increases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of nefazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 19. Nelfinavir and mifepristone may increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Nevirapine decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of nifedipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Mifepristone and nilotinib can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 23. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of nimodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norelgestromin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 25. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norethindrone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 26. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 27. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norgestimate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 28. Mifepristone and nortriptyline can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 29. Mifepristone and octreotide can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 30. Mifepristone and ofloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 31. Mifepristone and olanzapine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 32. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of oliceridine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 33. Mifepristone and ondansetron can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 34. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of osilodrostat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Both osilodrostat and mifepristone can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Osimertinib and mifepristone can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 36. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of ospemifene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Oxaliplatin increases the level or effect of mifepristone by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 38. Oxcarbazepine decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 39. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of oxycodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ozanimod and mifepristone can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 41. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of paclitaxel by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. 42. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of paclitaxel protein-bound by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. 43. Mifepristone and paliperidone can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 44. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of paricalcitol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Mifepristone and pasireotide can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 46. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of pazopanib by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. The combination may also increase the QT interval. Alternatives should be considered if available. 47. Mifepristone and pentamidine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 48. Pentobarbital decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 49. Mifepristone and perphenazine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 50. Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 51. Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 52. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of pioglitazone by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. 53. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 54. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of polatuzumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 55. Posaconazole increases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. The combination may also prolong the QT interval. Alternatives should be considered if available. 56. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of pravastatin by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 57. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of praziquantel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Primidone decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 59. Mifepristone and procainamide can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 60. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of progesterone intravaginal gel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of progesterone micronized by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of promethazine by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Mifepristone and propafenone can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 65. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of propofol by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Mifepristone and protriptyline can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 67. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of quazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Mifepristone and quetiapine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 69. Mifepristone and quinine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 70. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of quizartinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. When co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce quizartinib dosage to 4 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, interrupt quizartinib for the duration of inhibitor use. 71. Quizartinib and mifepristone may increase each other's effects on the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 72. Mifepristone and ranolazine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 73. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of repaglinide by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2C8/2C9; therefore, the smallest recommended doses for substrates should be used, and monitoring is advised. 74. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of resmetirom by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Reduce the dose of resmetirom (a CYP2C8 substrate) when co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 75. Ribociclib and mifepristone may increase each other's toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 76. Rifabutin decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 77. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 78. Rifapentine decreases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied, and co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 79. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of ripretinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor will increase systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 80. Mifepristone and risperidone can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and alternative treatments should be considered if available. 81. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
